issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) but the solution's Bookstore implementation defines init() with no parameters and attempts to assign self.books = books (an undefined identifier). Meanwhile, the solution's Client calls Bookstore(books: books). This constructor signature mismatch (and the undefined use of 'books' in the init) makes the solution inconsistent with the specification and will prevent successful compilation and correct implementation by students.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Bookstore initializer in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift to match the specification: implement init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books }. This aligns the Bookstore constructor with the problem statement and with the Client usage (Bookstore(books: books)). Ensure the parameter name and type match exactly.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book]). The client code (in the solution) constructs a Bookstore using Bookstore(books: books), but the Bookstore implementation in the solution defines init() with no parameter. This mismatch between the expected initializer name/signature and the actual implementation will confuse students about which initializer to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer match the problem statement and the client usage. Implement init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books } so the signature and parameter name align across the problem, template, and client code.
